items.title: 潜在雅可比引导：从预训练人形控制器中激发富接触的分布外行为
items.summary: 本文提出潜在雅可比引导（Latent Jacobian Steer，LJS），将直接关节动作空间的采样与冻结预训练全身人形控制器输入潜在空间的语义耦合起来，从而在仿真中搜索出跨栏、操作铰接物体、以非抓握接触开门等富接触分布外行为；在十组随机种子下，LJS 完成各人形任务的比例高于仅在动作空间或仅在潜在空间搜索，并能在四个装配任务上优于直接在目标空间搜索来引导目标条件灵巧手策略。
items.lede: 把动作空间采样与冻结策略的潜在语义耦合，让预训练人形控制器在仿真中做出跨栏、开门等训练分布外的富接触动作。

sections.background: 预训练的通用潜在条件全身人形控制器（行为基础模型，BFM）已能协调全身运动，但如何让其完成训练分布之外的复杂富接触任务仍是难题。直接在关节动作空间探索可针对任务调整，却容易破坏预训练策略学到的协调；在潜在空间探索能保留协调，却难以精确引导到期望的物理效果，两种探索空间各有短板。
sections.conclusion: 作者在多种分布外任务上验证：用 LJS 在仿真中搜索可产生跨栏、操作铰接物体、通过非抓握接触开门等富接触行为。十组随机种子下，LJS 在每个任务上的完成度都高于仅在动作空间或仅在潜在空间搜索；消融表明两种空间单独使用都不具备耦合后的能力。该方法还能引导目标条件灵巧手策略，在四个装配任务上优于直接在目标空间搜索。结论限于材料报告的仿真搜索设定，尚未给出真机部署结果。
sections.method: 输入是一个冻结的预训练潜在条件人形控制器，以及用期望物理效果描述的新任务。方法先在直接关节动作空间采样与任务相关的扰动，再通过策略雅可比的阻尼局部逆，把这些动作扰动映射为候选潜在指令 z。候选指令交由冻结策略执行，并按新任务所需的物理结果筛选和组合成潜在指令序列。已验证的改进来自动作空间采样与潜在空间语义的耦合：消融显示单独在任一空间搜索都达不到同等效果。
sections.takeaways: 若有人形机器人平台和已训练好的潜在条件全身控制器，可把 LJS 用作仿真中的任务搜索工具，为跨栏、开门、操作铰接物体等富接触技能生成潜在指令序列。所需条件是能访问冻结策略及其雅可比，并有可评估物理结果的仿真环境；灵巧手场景还需目标条件策略。距离真机部署仍缺真机验证、对仿真到现实差距的评估，以及搜索成本与实时性的验证。实测结论仅限材料报告的仿真任务与十组种子设定。

en.title: Latent Jacobian Steer: Eliciting Contact-Rich Out-of-Distribution Behaviors from Pretrained Humanoid Controllers
en.summary: This paper proposes Latent Jacobian Steer (LJS), which couples sampling in direct joint-action space with the semantics of the frozen pretrained whole-body humanoid controller's input latent space to search, in simulation, for contact-rich out-of-distribution behaviors such as hurdling, manipulating articulated objects, and opening doors through non-prehensile contact. Over ten seeds, LJS completes more of each humanoid task than searching in either action space or latent space alone, and it also steers a goal-conditioned dexterous hand policy through four assembly tasks better than searching directly in goal space.
en.lede: Coupling action-space sampling with the latent semantics of a frozen policy lets a pretrained humanoid controller produce out-of-distribution contact-rich behaviors such as hurdling and door opening in simulation.

sections.background: A pretrained general latent-conditioned whole-body humanoid controller, i.e., a behavioral foundation model (BFM), already coordinates whole-body motion, but eliciting complex contact-rich behaviors outside its training distribution remains difficult. Exploring directly in joint-action space allows task-specific adjustment but can disrupt the coordination learned by the pretrained controller, whereas latent-space exploration preserves that coordination but is hard to steer toward desired physical effects; each exploration space has complementary weaknesses.
sections.conclusion: Across diverse out-of-distribution tasks, simulation-based search with LJS produces contact-rich behaviors including hurdling, manipulating articulated objects, and opening doors through non-prehensile contact. Over ten seeds, LJS completes more of each humanoid task than searching in either action space or latent space alone, and ablations show neither space alone provides the capability of their coupling. The method also steers a goal-conditioned dexterous hand policy through four assembly tasks better than searching directly in goal space. These conclusions are limited to the simulation-based search setting reported in the material; no real-robot deployment results are given.
sections.method: The inputs are a frozen pretrained latent-conditioned humanoid controller and a new task specified through desired physical effects. The method first samples task-relevant perturbations in direct joint-action space, then maps them through a damped local inverse of the policy Jacobian to obtain candidate latent commands z. Candidate commands are executed through the frozen policy, and outcomes are evaluated in simulation and composed into latent-command sequences that accomplish the task. The verified improvement comes from coupling action-space sampling with latent-space semantics: ablations show searching in either space alone does not match the coupled approach.
sections.takeaways: Given a humanoid platform and an already trained latent-conditioned whole-body controller, LJS can serve as a simulation-based task-search tool to generate latent-command sequences for contact-rich skills such as hurdling, opening doors, and manipulating articulated objects. It requires access to the frozen policy and its Jacobian plus a simulator that can evaluate physical outcomes; the dexterous-hand setting additionally needs a goal-conditioned policy. Real-robot deployment still lacks real-world validation, an assessment of the simulation-to-reality gap, and verification of search cost and real-time feasibility. The measured conclusions are limited to the simulation tasks and ten-seed setting reported in the material.

items.original_title: Latent Jacobian Steer: Eliciting Contact-Rich Out-of-Distribution Behaviors from Pretrained Humanoid Controllers
items.original_summary: Given a pretrained general latent-conditioned whole-body humanoid controller, say a behavioral foundation model (BFM), how can we elicit complex and contact-rich out-of-distribution behaviors? Raw joint-action exploration enables direct, task-specific adjustments but can disrupt coordination learned by the pretrained controller, whereas latent exploration retains that coordination but is difficult to steer toward desired physical effects. To combine the complementary strengths of these exploration spaces, we propose Latent Jacobian Steer (LJS), which couples sampling in direct joint-action space with the semantics of the learned frozen controller's input latent space. For a task specified through desired physical effects, we sample task-relevant joint-action perturbations and map them through a damped local inverse of the policy Jacobian to obtain candidate latent ($z$) commands. These commands are executed through the frozen pretrained policy, while exploration is directed toward the physical outcomes required by the new task. Candidate outcomes are evaluated in simulation and composed into latent-command sequences that accomplish the task. Ablations show that neither action-space nor latent-space exploration alone provides the same capability as their coupling. Across diverse out-of-distribution tasks, simulation-based searching using this method produces contact-rich behaviors, including hurdling, manipulating articulated objects, and opening doors through non-prehensile contact. Over ten seeds, LJS completes more of each humanoid task than when searching in either space alone. Beyond humanoids, it also steers a goal-conditioned dexterous hand policy through four assembly tasks better than searching in goal space directly.

figure.caption: Figure 2: Latent Jacobian Steer overview. (A) CEM proposes joint-action perturbations Δ​u. (B) A damped inverse of the frozen policy Jacobian maps each proposal to a latent change Δ​z; the updated latent command is normalized and simulated through the pretrained controller. (C) Physical-effect scores rank the rollouts and guide CEM updates. The best admissible candidate is executed for a short window before replanning. The actor remains frozen throughout.

items.title: RoboDyna：在物理一致的动力学下评估机器人操作的基准
items.summary: RoboDyna 是一个面向动态场景的机器人操作基准，包含 20 个概念性动态任务（覆盖五类能力）和 10 个视觉与语义更丰富的家庭任务，提供 3,500 条专家演示、同步与异步两套评估协议，以及任务成功率和部分完成度指标。对视觉-语言-动作模型和一个世界-动作模型共 5.4K 个回合的评估显示，所有策略成功率均低于 20%；世界-动作模型能捕捉简单物理动力学，但在复杂交互上表现吃力，且预测保真度与任务成功并不总是一致；同步与异步对比中，推理延迟改变了 5–12% 回合的结果，但平均成功率变化不超过 3%；在同等条件下，人类基线大幅优于所有策略。
items.lede: 新基准 RoboDyna 用 20 个概念任务和 10 个家庭任务检验动态操作，5.4K 回合评估中所有策略成功率不足 20%，人类基线明显领先。

sections.background: 真实世界中的物体操作要求智能体理解环境如何运作与演化，并据此行动。现有基准难以同时满足这两点：偏物理的基准只评估预测保真度，不涉及闭环动作；动态操作基准常使用简化、物理上不合理的物体运动，难以检验真实动力学下的推理与行动。此外，评估通常是同步的，在推理时冻结环境，使计算耗时与任务结果无关，掩盖了实际部署中的延迟影响。
sections.conclusion: 在 5.4K 个评估回合中，所有被测策略的任务成功率都低于 20%，说明动态操作仍是明显短板。世界-动作模型能刻画简单物理动力学，但面对复杂交互时表现不佳，其预测保真度与任务成功之间也没有稳定对应关系。同步与异步评估的对比表明，推理延迟会翻转 5–12% 回合的成败，而平均成功率的变化最多为 3 个百分点；在匹配条件下，人类基线显著优于所有策略。这些结论限于该基准所报告的模拟设定与任务集合。
sections.method: 输入是动态场景中的视觉观测与任务指令，策略需要在环境持续演化时输出动作。RoboDyna 用两类任务组织评估：20 个概念性动态任务覆盖五类能力，采用两因素难度设计，物体简单、场景杂乱度低；另有 10 个家庭任务在视觉和语义更丰富的模拟真实环境中实例化同样的能力。基准提供 3,500 条专家演示，并配套同步与异步两套评估协议，分别对应推理时冻结环境和不冻结环境，同时报告任务成功率与部分完成度指标，还提供交互工具用于人类基线评估。已验证的改进来自评估设计本身：异步协议让推理延迟进入任务结果，从而暴露同步评估看不到的成败翻转；但材料未报告与旧基准的对照实验，因此不应据此宣称方法优于既有基准。
sections.takeaways: 若要在动态操作上使用该基准，需要具备可运行模拟环境与策略推理的硬件条件，并准备或使用其 3,500 条专家演示来训练和校准模型。对产业场景而言，当机器人需要在移动物体、变化场景中闭环决策时，可优先用异步协议评估，因为推理延迟可能翻转 5–12% 的回合结果，仅看平均成功率会低估这一风险。距离真机部署仍缺少真实机器人平台上的验证，现有结论只适用于该基准报告的模拟任务与设定；世界-动作模型的预测保真度不能替代任务成功率作为部署判据。

en.title: RoboDyna: A Benchmark for Evaluating Robotic Manipulation under Physically Grounded Dynamics
en.summary: RoboDyna is a benchmark for robotic manipulation in dynamic scenes. It contains 20 conceptual dynamic tasks spanning five capability categories and 10 household tasks in visually and semantically richer simulated environments, with 3,500 expert demonstrations, paired synchronous and asynchronous evaluation protocols, and metrics for task success and partial completion. Across 5.4K episodes evaluating vision-language-action models and a world-action model, all policies achieve success rates below 20%. The world-action model captures simple physical dynamics but struggles with complex interactions, and its prediction fidelity does not consistently align with task success. Sync-async comparisons show that inference latency flips 5–12% of episode outcomes while changing average success rates by at most 3%. Human baselines substantially outperform all policies under matched conditions.
en.lede: The new RoboDyna benchmark tests dynamic manipulation with 20 conceptual and 10 household tasks; across 5.4K episodes all policies stay below 20% success, while human baselines lead clearly.

sections.background: Manipulating objects in the dynamic real world requires understanding how the environment functions and evolves and acting accordingly. Existing benchmarks do not adequately cover both needs: physics-oriented benchmarks evaluate predictive fidelity but not closed-loop action, while dynamic manipulation benchmarks often use simplified, physically implausible object motions, limiting evaluation of reasoning and action under realistic dynamics. Evaluation is also typically synchronized, freezing the environment during inference so that computation time is irrelevant to task outcomes and the effect of latency is hidden.
sections.conclusion: Across 5.4K evaluated episodes, all tested policies achieve task success rates below 20%, showing that dynamic manipulation remains a clear weakness. The world-action model captures simple physical dynamics but struggles with complex interactions, and its prediction fidelity does not consistently correspond to task success. Sync-async comparisons show that inference latency flips 5–12% of episode outcomes while changing average success rates by at most 3 percentage points. Under matched conditions, human baselines substantially outperform all policies. These conclusions are limited to the simulated settings and task sets reported by the benchmark.
sections.method: The input is visual observation and a task instruction in a dynamic scene, and the policy must output actions while the environment keeps evolving. RoboDyna organizes evaluation around two task sets: 20 conceptual dynamic tasks spanning five capability categories under a two-factor difficulty design with simple objects and minimal scene clutter, and 10 household tasks that instantiate the same capabilities in visually and semantically richer simulated real-world environments. The benchmark provides 3,500 expert demonstrations, paired synchronous and asynchronous evaluation protocols that respectively freeze or do not freeze the environment during inference, metrics for task success and partial completion, and interactive tools for human baseline evaluation. The verified improvement comes from the evaluation design itself: the asynchronous protocol lets inference latency affect task outcomes and exposes outcome flips that synchronized evaluation cannot see; the material reports no comparison against prior benchmarks, so no claim of superiority over existing methods is made.
sections.takeaways: Using this benchmark requires a runnable simulation environment and hardware for policy inference, plus its 3,500 expert demonstrations for training and calibration. For industrial settings where robots must make closed-loop decisions among moving objects and changing scenes, the asynchronous protocol is the more informative choice, because inference latency can flip 5–12% of episode outcomes and average success rates alone understate this risk. Validation on real robot platforms is still missing, and the reported conclusions apply only to the simulated tasks and settings of this benchmark; prediction fidelity of a world-action model cannot replace task success as a deployment criterion.

items.original_title: RoboDyna: A Benchmark for Evaluating Robotic Manipulation under Physically Grounded Dynamics
items.original_summary: Object manipulation in the dynamic real world requires understanding how the environment functions and evolves, and acting accordingly. Existing benchmarks, however, do not adequately address these needs. Physics-oriented benchmarks evaluate predictive fidelity but not closed-loop action. Dynamic robotic manipulation benchmarks often use simplified, physically implausible object motions, limiting evaluation of reasoning and action under realistic dynamics. Evaluation is also typically synchronized, freezing the environment during inference and making computation time irrelevant to task outcomes. en.title: Learning a Food World Model That Predicts the Next State from Production Data
en.summary: Food assembly robots pick ingredients from a pan, and every pick must deliver a target weight. We learn a world model of food picking from 61,773 production picks, labeled automatically by a camera and a scale (self-supervised learning). From the pre-pick heightmap of the pan on a 2.5 mm grid, the commanded pick action, the food and the utensil, the model predicts the post-pick heightmap and the picked mass with uncertainty. We evaluate the mass prediction on 12,294 held-out picks of nine foods. The production controller keeps each pick near its commanded target. The model's root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 10.93 g is 9% lower than that of the commanded target or of a per-food mean. This RMSE is 24% lower than that of the controller's internal mass estimate. Gradient-boosted trees on 20 hand-crafted features have a 0.2 g lower RMSE, but they predict only the mass, not the next state that planning and policy learning need. Using the predicted uncertainty, we decline the most uncertain picks and answer 89.4% of picks with an RMSE of 10.28 g. The prediction barely responds to the commanded volume and depth, because they vary little in closed-loop production. The model also fails without warning at target weights not seen in training. Future directions include action-primitive conditioning and a more general model across foods and utensils. We give recommendations for learning world models from production data.
en.lede: Food assembly robots pick ingredients from a pan, and each pick must meet a target weight. Researchers learned a world model from 61,773 production picks that predicts the post-pick heightmap and mass, and validated its accuracy and uncertainty handling on held-out data.

sections.background: Food assembly robots need to pick ingredients from a pan and ensure each pick meets a target weight. However, learning a world model from production data that predicts post-pick states (such as heightmap and picked mass) faces challenges: actions vary little in production, and the model must handle uncertainty. Existing approaches like the controller's internal estimate or hand-crafted feature models have limitations in accuracy or functionality.
sections.conclusion: The model achieves an RMSE of 10.93 g for mass prediction on 12,294 held-out picks, 9% lower than the commanded target or a per-food mean, and 24% lower than the controller's internal estimate. Gradient-boosted trees have a 0.2 g lower RMSE but predict only mass. By using uncertainty to decline the most uncertain picks, it answers 89.4% of picks with an RMSE of 10.28 g. The prediction barely responds to commanded volume and depth, and it fails without warning at unseen target weights.
sections.method: The input is the pre-pick heightmap of the pan on a 2.5 mm grid, the commanded pick action, the food and the utensil; the output is the post-pick heightmap and the picked mass with uncertainty. The model is trained via self-supervised learning from 61,773 production picks, with labels automatically generated by a camera and a scale. Core modules include heightmap encoding and action-conditioned prediction, along with uncertainty estimation to support rejection decisions. The verified improvement comes from using uncertainty to decline the most uncertain picks, thereby reducing RMSE while maintaining high coverage.
sections.takeaways: This world model can be applied to food assembly robots, requiring a camera and a scale to automatically label production data and collecting a large number of pick samples. If deployed on a real robot, it is necessary to validate the model's generalization in scenarios with more varied actions and to address the failure at unseen target weights. The current conclusions are limited to the closed-loop production setting, where commanded volume and depth vary little and the variety of foods and utensils is limited. Future work needs to introduce action-primitive conditioning and a general model across foods and utensils.

items.title: HumanoidPose：面向人形机器人的单目三维姿态估计
items.summary: 该工作针对人形机器人三维全身姿态估计这一空白，提出基准数据集 Humanoids 与框架 HumanoidPose。Humanoids 提供多形态人形机器人的合成三维监督、真实场景人工标注二维数据，以及在实体 Roban 人形机器人上采集的 RGB 序列与机器人状态配对数据，用于三维评测。HumanoidPose 将类人视觉感知、机器人关节建模与显式运动学约束结合。在 Humanoids 与 DHRP-H1 基准上的实验显示，该方法在关节恢复与三维姿态估计上表现良好，并支持零样本迁移到真实二维与三维评测；消融实验表明机器人原生关节建模与显式运动学约束均有贡献。
items.lede: 新基准 Humanoids 与框架 HumanoidPose 尝试用人形机器人自身的关节结构约束单目三维姿态估计，并在实体 Roban 上完成零样本评测。

sections.background: 人形机器人正越来越多地进入真实环境，仅凭单目图像恢复其全身三维姿态，对外部状态感知、运动分析和机器人学习都很重要。但人形机器人姿态估计（HRPE）处在传统机器人姿态估计（RPE）与人体姿态估计（HPE）的交汇处：RPE 主要面向非人形机器人，尤其是固定基座机械臂；HPE 则建立在人类特有的骨架拓扑、人体模型和运动先验之上。因此，现有两类范式都不能完整覆盖该任务，人形机器人原生的三维姿态恢复研究不足，也缺少配套训练数据与评测协议的专用基准。
sections.conclusion: 作者构建了 Humanoids 基准，并提供 HumanoidPose 框架。Humanoids 包含多形态人形机器人的合成三维监督、真实场景人工标注二维数据，以及实体 Roban 人形机器人上 RGB 序列与机器人状态配对的三维评测数据。在 Humanoids 与 DHRP-H1 基准上，方法在关节恢复和三维姿态估计上表现良好，并实现零样本迁移到真实二维与三维评测。消融实验显示，机器人原生关节建模与显式运动学约束都对性能有贡献。
sections.method: 输入是单目图像，输出是人形机器人的三维全身姿态。框架把类人视觉感知与机器人关节建模结合起来，并用显式运动学约束把预测的姿态锚定到机器人自身的关节结构上，而不是直接套用人体骨架与人体模型。消融实验表明，机器人原生关节建模和显式运动学约束是已验证的改进来源；材料未报告与旧方法的直接对照，因此其相对优势应限定在上述实验设定内理解。
sections.takeaways: 在条件具备时，该方法可用于人形机器人的外部状态监测、动作分析和示教数据采集等场景，例如用固定相机观察实体机器人并恢复其三维姿态。它需要单目 RGB 输入，训练阶段依赖合成三维监督与人工标注二维数据，三维评测依赖与机器人状态配对的真实序列。距离更广泛的真机部署，仍需在更多机型、更多真实场景和不同光照与遮挡条件下验证零样本三维精度，并确认运动学参数变化时的鲁棒性。

en.title: HumanoidPose: Monocular 3D Pose Estimation for Humanoid Robots
en.summary: This work addresses the gap in 3D whole-body pose estimation for humanoid robots by introducing Humanoids, a benchmark, and HumanoidPose, a framework. Humanoids provides synthetic 3D supervision across diverse humanoid embodiments, manually annotated real-world 2D data, and real-world RGB sequences paired with robot states for 3D evaluation on a physical Roban humanoid. HumanoidPose combines human-inspired visual perception with robot articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding. Experiments on Humanoids and the DHRP-H1 benchmark show strong performance in articulation recovery and 3D pose estimation, including zero-shot transfer to real-world 2D and 3D evaluation; ablations show contributions from robot-native articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding.
en.lede: A new benchmark, Humanoids, and a framework, HumanoidPose, use the robot's own articulation structure to constrain monocular 3D pose estimation, with zero-shot evaluation on a physical Roban humanoid.

sections.background: As humanoid robots increasingly enter real-world environments, recovering their 3D whole-body pose from monocular imagery is important for external state perception, motion analysis, and robot learning. However, Humanoid Robot Pose Estimation (HRPE) sits at the intersection of conventional Robot Pose Estimation (RPE) and Human Pose Estimation (HPE), and neither paradigm fully addresses it: RPE mainly targets non-humanoid robots, especially fixed-base manipulators, while HPE relies on human-specific skeletal topologies, body models, and motion priors. Consequently, humanoid-native 3D pose recovery remains insufficiently studied, and a dedicated benchmark with suitable training data and evaluation protocols is lacking.
sections.conclusion: The authors build the Humanoids benchmark and propose the HumanoidPose framework. Humanoids contains synthetic 3D supervision across diverse humanoid embodiments, manually annotated real-world 2D data, and real-world RGB sequences paired with robot states for 3D evaluation on a physical Roban humanoid. On Humanoids and the DHRP-H1 benchmark, the method performs strongly in articulation recovery and 3D pose estimation and achieves zero-shot transfer to real-world 2D and 3D evaluation. Ablation studies show that robot-native articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding both contribute to performance.
sections.method: The input is a monocular image, and the output is the robot's 3D whole-body pose. The framework combines human-inspired visual perception with robot articulation modeling and uses explicit kinematic grounding to anchor predicted pose to the robot's own joint structure rather than directly applying human skeletons and body models. Ablations identify robot-native articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding as verified sources of improvement; the material reports no direct comparison against prior methods, so relative advantages should be understood within the reported experimental settings.
sections.takeaways: Where the required conditions hold, the method could support external state monitoring, motion analysis, and demonstration data collection for humanoid robots, for example observing a physical robot with a fixed camera and recovering its 3D pose. items.original_title: HumanoidPose: Monocular 3D Pose Estimation for Humanoid Robots
items.original_summary: As humanoid robots increasingly enter real-world environments, recovering their 3D whole-body pose from monocular imagery is becoming increasingly important for external state perception, motion analysis, and robot learning. HumanoidPose combines human-inspired visual perception with robot articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding. Experiments on Humanoids and the DHRP-H1 benchmark demonstrate strong performance in articulation recovery and 3D pose estimation, including zero-shot transfer to real-world 2D and 3D evaluation. Ablation studies further show the contribution of robot-native articulation modeling and explicit kinematic grounding. The dataset and code will be publicly released to support future research in the community.

en.title: Instant-LIVO: Efficient LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry with Compact Geometry and a Bounded Single-Reference-Frame Map
en.summary: Instant-LIVO is a tightly coupled, high-speed, real-time LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry (LIVO) system for resource-constrained platforms. It uses a compact geometric map based on spatially hashed OctVox and cache-assisted heuristic staged K-nearest-neighbor searches to accelerate local-neighborhood retrieval and plane fitting, and a bounded single-reference-frame visual map with Schmidt-type uncertainty-aware photometric fusion to preserve correlation between the reference pose and the current state. On 32 public benchmarks and custom datasets, it achieves average processing-speed improvements of approximately 2.3x and 2.1x on X86 and ARM platforms, respectively, and reduces peak memory to approximately 1/20 and 1/13, with competitive accuracy against existing LIO and LIVO baselines.
en.lede: Instant-LIVO combines a compact geometric map with a bounded single-reference-frame visual map, improving LIVO processing speed by approximately 2.3x and 2.1x on X86 and ARM platforms and reducing peak memory to approximately 1/20 and 1/13.

sections.background: LIVO is a fundamental technology for autonomous systems, but fusing LiDAR, camera, and inertial data is computationally and memory intensive, making real-time deployment difficult on embedded or mobile platforms with limited compute and memory. Existing systems often trade accuracy against efficiency, motivating compact map representations, faster neighborhood queries, and bounded visual map size.
sections.conclusion: Evaluated on 32 public benchmarks and custom datasets, Instant-LIVO improves average processing speed by approximately 2.3x and 2.1x on X86 and ARM platforms, respectively, and reduces peak memory to approximately 1/20 and 1/13, while maintaining competitive accuracy and outperforming existing LIO and LIVO baselines in both accuracy and computational efficiency. These conclusions are limited to the benchmark and custom-data settings reported in the material.
sections.method: The system takes LiDAR point clouds, inertial measurement unit (IMU) data, and camera images as input and performs tightly coupled fusion in the order of IMU prediction, LiDAR geometric correction, and visual photometric correction. On the geometric side, it builds a compact map with spatially hashed OctVox and accelerates local-neighborhood retrieval and plane fitting using cache-assisted heuristic staged K-nearest-neighbor searches. On the visual side, it maintains a bounded single-reference-frame map, adaptively updates the reference frame according to tracking status, and uses Schmidt-type uncertainty-aware photometric fusion to retain correlation between the reference pose and the current state. The material provides no per-module ablation, so the speed and memory gains stem from the overall system design rather than causal validation of individual modules.
sections.takeaways: For deployment on compute- and memory-constrained platforms such as drones, handheld devices, or small mobile robots, the system could sustain real-time LIVO operation with lower peak memory, provided hardware synchronization and temporal calibration among LiDAR, camera, and IMU are available. Its gains are reported on 32 public benchmarks and custom datasets on X86 and ARM platforms; robustness in dynamic scenes, long-duration runs, and extreme lighting still needs validation. Real-robot deployment still requires verification of long-term stability on embedded platforms, degraded-sensor scenarios, and closed-loop control tasks.

items.original_title: Instant-LIVO: Efficient LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry with Compact Geometry and a Bounded Single-Reference-Frame Map
items.original_summary: LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry (LIVO) is a fundamental technology for autonomous systems; however, deployment on resource-constrained platforms remains challenging due to physical limitations. This paper presents Instant-LIVO, a tightly coupled, high-speed, real-time LIVO system. The system introduces a compact geometric map based on spatial-hashed OctVox and accelerates local-neighborhood retrieval and plane fitting through cache-assisted heuristic staged K-nearest-neighbor searches. It also employs a bounded single-reference-frame visual map that adaptively updates the reference frame according to the tracking status, while using Schmidt-type uncertainty-aware photometric fusion to maintain the correlation between the reference pose and the current state. The system performs multisensor fusion through a sequential process consisting of IMU prediction, LiDAR geometric correction, and visual photometric correction. It was evaluated on 32 public benchmarks and custom datasets. While maintaining competitive accuracy on both X86 and ARM platforms, Instant-LIVO achieves average processing-speed improvements of approximately 2.3x and 2.1x, respectively, and reduces peak memory usage to approximately 1/20 and 1/13, respectively. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing LIO and LIVO baselines in both accuracy and computational efficiency.The implementation is available at: https://github.com/Faker-0714/Instant-LIVO.git.

items.title: Mem-X：面向视觉—语言导航的记忆依赖型跨回合基准
items.summary: Mem-X 是一个用于评估“记忆依赖型”跨回合视觉—语言导航（VLN）的基准。它把多个回合组织成会话，后续指令会引用先前回合中见过的物体或路线，从而区分导航成功究竟依赖历史记忆还是当前探索。基准包含三个层级，分别考察历史物体回忆、记忆内定位与回合索引，以及脱离记忆的重定位与历史路线复现；后两级只提供回合内位姿、不提供回合坐标系之间的变换，要求智能体自行建立与历史记忆的空间对应。Mem-X 覆盖 34 个场景、710 个会话、共 2,071 个回合，其中 1,204 个为记忆依赖回合。作者还提出模块化基线 MemBridge，将语义场景记忆、跨回合定位和由粗到细的检索组合起来，以支持现有 VLN 智能体。实验显示 MemBridge 带来收益，同时表明记忆依赖导航仍有很大提升空间。
items.lede: Mem-X 把导航回合串成会话，让后续指令指向先前见过的物体或路线，从而检验智能体是否真的依赖记忆而非现场探索。

sections.background: 长期记忆让具身智能体能够跨任务复用过去的观察，但现有跨回合 VLN 基准往往无法判断导航成功究竟来自历史记忆还是当前探索。若不能把这两种来源分开，就难以衡量智能体是否真正记住了先前会话中的物体与路线，也难以比较不同记忆机制的效果。
sections.conclusion: Mem-X 用会话组织回合，使后续指令引用先前回合的物体或路线，并设置三个层级分别考察历史物体回忆、记忆内定位与回合索引、脱离记忆的重定位与历史路线复现。基准共 2,071 个回合、710 个会话、34 个场景，其中 1,204 个为记忆依赖回合。实验表明 MemBridge 能为现有先进 VLN 方法带来收益，但记忆依赖导航仍有明显提升空间。
sections.method: 输入是同一会话内按顺序到来的多个导航回合：每个回合给出指令和回合内位姿，但后两级不提供回合坐标系之间的变换。MemBridge 首先构建语义场景记忆，把历史观察按语义组织保存；然后进行跨回合定位，让当前回合与历史记忆建立空间对应；最后用由粗到细的检索从记忆中找回相关物体或路线，供现有 VLN 智能体使用。已验证的改进来自把这三部分组合成模块化基线后对现有先进 VLN 方法的支持；材料未报告与旧方法在同等设定下的逐项对照，因此其收益应理解为该基准设定下的实验观察。
sections.takeaways: 若要在真实服务机器人或仓储机器人上复用跨楼层、跨房间的先前观察，需要具备持续建图与语义记忆存储的硬件与数据条件，并能在回合间保持位姿估计。Mem-X 目前是仿真基准，距离真机部署还缺真实传感器噪声、长期记忆容量与跨会话漂移等验证。其结论仅适用于材料报告的 34 个场景与 2,071 个回合设定，不能直接外推到开放世界。若后续在真机上验证跨回合定位与检索的鲁棒性，才可考虑把 MemBridge 式模块接入实际 VLN 系统。

en.title: Mem-X: A Memory-Dependent Cross-Episode Benchmark for Vision-and-Language Navigation
en.summary: Mem-X is a benchmark for evaluating memory-dependent cross-episode vision-and-language navigation (VLN). It organizes episodes into sessions in which later instructions refer to objects or routes encountered in earlier episodes, making it possible to separate success that relies on historical memory from success driven by current exploration. The benchmark has three levels: historical-object recall, in-memory localization and episodic indexing, and off-memory relocalization and historical-route reproduction. For the latter two levels, agents receive episode-local poses but no transformations between episode frames, so they must establish spatial correspondence with historical memory themselves. Mem-X contains 2,071 episodes across 710 sessions in 34 scenes, including 1,204 memory-dependent episodes. The authors also provide MemBridge, a modular baseline that combines semantic scene memory, cross-episode localization, and coarse-to-fine retrieval to support existing VLN agents. Experiments show benefits from MemBridge while revealing substantial room for improvement on memory-dependent navigation.
en.lede: Mem-X chains navigation episodes into sessions and makes later instructions refer to previously seen objects or routes, testing whether agents truly rely on memory rather than on-site exploration.

sections.background: Long-term memory allows embodied agents to reuse past observations across tasks, but existing cross-episode VLN benchmarks often leave it unclear whether successful navigation relies on historical memory or on current exploration. Without separating these two sources, it is hard to measure whether an agent truly remembers objects and routes from earlier sessions, or to compare different memory mechanisms.
sections.conclusion: Mem-X organizes episodes into sessions so that later instructions refer to objects or routes from earlier episodes, and its three levels evaluate historical-object recall, in-memory localization and episodic indexing, and off-memory relocalization and historical-route reproduction. The benchmark comprises 2,071 episodes across 710 sessions in 34 scenes, including 1,204 memory-dependent episodes. Experiments show that MemBridge benefits state-of-the-art VLN methods, while memory-dependent navigation still has substantial room for improvement.
sections.method: The input is a sequence of navigation episodes within one session: each episode provides an instruction and an episode-local pose, but the latter two levels provide no transformation between episode frames. MemBridge first builds a semantic scene memory that stores historical observations in a semantically organized form; it then performs cross-episode localization to establish spatial correspondence between the current episode and historical memory; finally, coarse-to-fine retrieval recovers relevant objects or routes from memory for use by existing VLN agents. items.original_title: Mem-X: A Memory-Dependent Cross-Episode Benchmark for Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.original_summary: Long-term memory enables embodied agents to reuse past observations across tasks. We introduce Mem-X, a benchmark designed to evaluate memory-dependent cross-episode VLN. Mem-X organizes episodes into sessions in which subsequent instructions refer to objects or routes encountered in earlier episodes. Its three levels evaluate historical-object recall, in-memory localization and episodic indexing, and off-memory relocalization and historical-route reproduction. For the latter two levels, agents receive episode-local poses but no transformations between episode frames, requiring them to establish spatial correspondence with historical memory. We also provide MemBridge, a modular baseline that combines semantic scene memory, cross-episode localization, and coarse-to-fine retrieval to support existing VLN agents. Experiments with state-of-the-art VLN methods demonstrate the benefits of MemBridge while revealing substantial room for improvement on memory-dependent navigation. items.title: ScaleEvals：通过无重置自主玩耍扩展通用策略评估
items.summary: 通用机器人策略的真实世界评估受限于人工重置、人工评分以及诊断覆盖有限的小型固定任务集。ScaleEvals 提出一种可扩展的无重置评估协议，让策略在机器人集群上通过连续物理玩耍接受评估。视觉语言模型（VLM）自动提示器生成有场景依据的任务，并给出难度估计、语言提示和技能标签，从而支持跨多样 rollout 的性能分析；VLM 自动评分器评估任务进度，与人工评分者的一致率达到 90.7%。分数通过软胜 Bradley-Terry 模型聚合，标签分层方差分析（ANOVA）提供可解释的能力诊断。在 DROID 和 YAM 上超过 3,000 次物理自主 rollout 中，ScaleEvals 每工位每小时净完成 23.0 次 rollout，并将主动人工劳动减少 98%。对五个最先进通用策略排序时，ScaleEvals 在 DROID 上与留出的人工评估排名相关（r=0.94，rho=0.90，p=0.018），并在第二个本体 YAM 上保持内部一致（r=0.839，rho=0.80）。除总体排名外，研究还观察到行为组合性：重组动词、技能和物体条件证据可预测策略在未见提示上的顺序。在 10 个任务和 240 次前瞻性物理 rollout 中，恢复三策略排序的成对一致率为 96%，表明 ScaleEvals 不仅能预测哪个策略领先，还能预测排名在何处反转。

en.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
en.summary: Real-world evaluation of generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites with limited diagnostic coverage. ScaleEvals presents a scalable reset-free protocol that evaluates policies through continuous physical play across a robot fleet. A vision-language model (VLM) AutoPrompter generates scene-grounded tasks with difficulty estimates, language prompts, and skill tags, enabling performance analysis across diverse rollouts. A VLM AutoGrader assesses task progress and achieves 90.7% agreement with human graders. Scores are aggregated via a soft-win Bradley-Terry model, while tag-stratified ANOVA provides interpretable capability diagnostics. Across 3,000+ physical autonomous rollouts on DROID and YAM, ScaleEvals achieves 23.0 net rollouts/hr per station while reducing active human labor by 98%. When ranking five state-of-the-art generalist policies, ScaleEvals correlates with held-out manual evaluation ranking on DROID (r=0.94, rho=0.90, p=0.018) and remains internally consistent on a second embodiment, YAM (r=0.839, rho=0.80). Beyond aggregate rankings, behavioral compositionality is observed: recombining verb-, skill-, and object-conditioned evidence predicts policy order on unseen prompts. Across 10 tasks and 240 prospective physical rollouts, three-policy orderings are recovered with 96% pairwise concordance, showing that ScaleEvals can predict not just which policy leads, but where rankings reverse.
en.lede: ScaleEvals replaces manual resets and grading with continuous autonomous play across a robot fleet, completing 3,000+ physical rollouts on DROID and YAM and producing policy rankings that correlate strongly with human evaluation.

items.title: 面向自主机器人应用的实时神经形态听觉与视觉感知：在漫游车平台上的集成与实验评估
items.summary: 该技术报告展示了一台四轮漫游车平台，同时集成三条实时感知流水线：基于预训练音频神经网络（PANNs）并运行在 NVIDIA Jetson GPU 上的传统音频分类流水线；将脉冲神经网络（SNN）部署在 SynSense Xylo Audio 2 芯片上的神经形态音频流水线；以及用事件相机采集事件、由 SpikeYOLO 脉冲检测器处理以检测交通锥的神经形态视觉流水线。在 Xylo 芯片上，从麦克风信号到低音与高音分类的整个处理链均在片上完成，主机只负责配置设备并读取输出神经元。所有模型以容器化服务部署并通过 ROS 2 集成，可配置的动作调度器将检测类别映射为机器人行为，闭合感知与执行回路。平台在概念验证场景中演示：机器人对两条音频流水线检测到的声音类别作出反应，并用事件相机检测交通锥，表明将神经形态硬件集成到实时运行的多模态机器人平台具有可行性。
items.lede: 一台四轮漫游车把传统音频分类、片上脉冲神经网络音频分类和事件相机交通锥检测三条实时流水线通过 ROS 2 集成，演示了神经形态硬件进入多模态机器人平台的可行性。

sections.background: 移动机器人需要持续运行感知，且受严格延迟与能耗约束；神经形态感知与计算被视为替代传统深度学习流水线的有前景方案。但多数神经形态方案仍在离线或孤立基准上评估，将其集成进完整机器人系统的探索仍然有限。

sections.method: 输入包括麦克风音频信号和事件相机输出的事件流。传统音频分支用预训练音频神经网络（PANNs）在 NVIDIA Jetson GPU 上做音频分类；神经形态音频分支把脉冲神经网络（SNN）部署在 SynSense Xylo Audio 2 芯片上，从麦克风信号到低音与高音分类全部在片上完成，主机仅配置设备并读取输出神经元；神经形态视觉分支用 SpikeYOLO 脉冲检测器处理事件相机数据以检测交通锥。三条流水线均以容器化服务部署，通过 ROS 2 集成，并由可配置的动作调度器把检测类别映射为机器人行为，从而闭合感知与执行回路。已验证的改进来自系统集成与实时运行演示，材料未报告与旧方法的对照性能比较。
sections.takeaways: 该平台适合需要低延迟、低功耗持续感知的移动机器人场景，例如用声音类别触发行为、用事件相机检测交通锥等目标；部署需要 ROS 2 环境、NVIDIA Jetson GPU、SynSense Xylo Audio 2 芯片与事件相机等硬件条件。若要把此类神经形态流水线用于真实任务，还需在更多场景与更长运行时间下验证稳定性、延迟和能耗，并补充与常规深度学习流水线的定量对照。当前结论仅限材料报告的概念验证设定，不能外推为已优于传统方法。

sections.takeaways: 该平台适合需要低延迟、低功耗持续感知的移动机器人场景，例如用声音类别触发行为、用事件相机检测交通锥等目标；部署需要 ROS 2 环境、NVIDIA Jetson GPU、SynSense Xylo Audio 2 芯片与事件相机等硬件条件。若要把此类神经形态流水线用于真实任务，还需在更多场景与更长运行时间下验证稳定性、延迟和能耗，并补充与常规深度学习流水线的定量对照。当前结论仅限材料报告的概念验证设定，不能外推为已优于传统方法。

en.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
en.summary: This technical report presents a four-wheel rover platform that combines three real-time perception pipelines: a classical audio tagging pipeline based on Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) running on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU; a neuromorphic audio pipeline in which a spiking neural network (SNN) is deployed on the SynSense Xylo Audio 2 chip; and a neuromorphic vision pipeline in which events from an event-based camera are processed by the SpikeYOLO spiking detector for traffic cone detection. On the Xylo chip, the entire processing chain from the microphone signal to the classification of low- and high-pitched sounds runs on-chip, while the host only configures the device and reads the output neurons. All models are deployed as containerised services and integrated through ROS 2, and a configurable action dispatcher maps detected classes to robot behaviours, closing the loop between perception and actuation. The platform is demonstrated in a proof-of-concept scenario in which the robot reacts to sound classes detected by both audio pipelines and detects traffic cones with the event camera, showing the feasibility of integrating neuromorphic hardware into a multimodal robotic platform operating in real time.
en.lede: A four-wheel rover integrates classical audio tagging, on-chip spiking neural network audio classification, and event-camera traffic cone detection through ROS 2, demonstrating that neuromorphic hardware can enter a multimodal robotic platform.

sections.background: Mobile robots must run perception continuously under tight latency and energy constraints, and neuromorphic sensing and computing are seen as a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored.
sections.conclusion: The report integrates three real-time perception pipelines on a four-wheel rover platform and demonstrates them in a proof-of-concept scenario: classical PANNs audio tagging runs on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, SNN-based audio classification runs entirely on-chip on the SynSense Xylo Audio 2, and SpikeYOLO detects traffic cones on event-camera data. All models are deployed as containerised services and integrated through ROS 2, and an action dispatcher maps detected classes to robot behaviours; the robot reacts to sound classes detected by both audio pipelines and detects traffic cones, showing that neuromorphic hardware can be integrated into a multimodal robotic platform in real time.
sections.method: The inputs are microphone audio signals and event streams from an event-based camera. The classical audio branch uses Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU for audio tagging; the neuromorphic audio branch deploys a spiking neural network (SNN) on the SynSense Xylo Audio 2 chip, where the whole chain from microphone signal to low- and high-pitched sound classification runs on-chip while the host only configures the device and reads output neurons; the neuromorphic vision branch uses the SpikeYOLO spiking detector on event-camera data to detect traffic cones. All three pipelines are deployed as containerised services, integrated through ROS 2, and connected to robot behaviours by a configurable action dispatcher, closing the perception-actuation loop. The verified improvement comes from system integration and a real-time demonstration; the material reports no controlled performance comparison against prior methods.
sections.takeaways: The platform targets mobile robot scenarios that need low-latency, low-power continuous perception, such as triggering behaviours from sound classes or detecting targets like traffic cones with an event camera; deployment requires a ROS 2 environment, an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, a SynSense Xylo Audio 2 chip, and an event-based camera. Before such neuromorphic pipelines can be used in real tasks, stability, latency, and energy use must be validated across more scenarios and longer runs, and quantitative comparisons with conventional deep learning pipelines are needed. The conclusions are limited to the proof-of-concept setting reported in the material and should not be extrapolated as outperforming conventional methods.
